Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-09 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (AE, Redwood), Omar (SE, Redwood), Rachel (CS, Redwood), Lena (Head of ML, Equinox), Samir (CTO, Equinox), Priya (Infra Lead, Equinox)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:00:05] Lena: Yeah, I'm Lena, Head of ML at Equinox, we run customer analytics and some internal agents.
[00:00:09] Samir: Samir here, CTO, mostly listening today, high level budget and infra questions.
[00:00:13] Priya: Priya, infra lead. I'll be owning any dedicated/private deploys.
[00:00:17] Maya: Awesome. Omar, you want to say quick hello?
[00:00:19] Omar: Hey all, Omar Patel, solutions engineer at Redwood. I'll dig into perf and cost levers.
[00:00:24] Rachel: Rachel from CS, here to help coordinate pilot.

[00:00:30] Maya: Goal for today's call is to understand your budget, token volumes, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense given cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:00:38] Lena: High level — we're evaluating LLMs to power summarization and a conversational assistant. Typical request is 1–3k tokens input, output 200–500 tokens. Peak concurrency around 120–150 qps, average maybe 40 qps. We're cost sensitive; board put a soft limit of about $30k per month for inference.
[00:00:57] Omar: got it. is that 120 qps at what concurrency — approximate parallel requests?
[00:01:02] Priya: Peak concurrent requests ~150, we have autoscaling on our app side but want the inference layer to behave predictably.

[00:01:10] Samir: Quick question up front: what's Redwood's hosted per-token baseline for common open models? ballpark numbers.
[00:01:16] Maya: Sure, ballpark for hosted: for a medium-sized LLM family (quantized 4-bit variants) you're looking at roughly $0.0008 to $0.0018 per input+output token depending on model size and latency SLO. smaller models can be down to ~$0.0004 per token. those are hosted API list rates — committed discounts and warm caches change numbers.
[00:01:39] Lena: okay, that range is a bit wide. at 40 qps avg and let's say 1,200 tokens per transaction total, that would be... hmm math, 40 * 1200 * 30 days = 1,440,000 tokens/day? wait that's off.
[00:01:55] Omar: quick calc: 40 requests/sec * 1200 tokens = 48k tokens/sec. times 3600 = 172.8M tokens/hour. times 24 ~ 4.1B tokens/day — that's if 24/7. but your traffic probably not 24/7 at peak.
[00:02:10] Priya: correct, peak is not sustained. our average monthly token volume looks like ~600M tokens/month today per product, but could grow 2-3x in 6 months.
[00:02:18] Maya: great, that helps. so at 600M tokens/mo at $0.0008/token hosted that's $480k/mo — so hosted without batching/caching would be way over your $30k target.
[00:02:29] Lena: yeah that's the core of the question: how do we get to something like $30k? is Dedicated or Private the only path? or can batching/caching get us there on hosted?
[00:02:38] Omar: there are multiple levers. short answer: batching + prefix/KV caching + model choice and quantization are the biggest multipliers. with aggressive batching and KV cache hit rates you can reduce effective token bill by 3-10x compared to naive per-token billing. also Dedicated reserved capacity changes the economics because you buy GPU capacity and amortize across tokens.
[00:02:56] Maya: to add, we offer autoscaling dedicated pools and you can pin a model variant; plus dedicated can be 40–60% cheaper per-effective-token in many cases versus hosted listed rates depending on utilization. Private has higher upfront infra/license costs but gives you full control and potentially cheapest long-term rate if you have high sustained usage.

[00:03:15] [00:03:15] Lena: can you unpack the caching numbers? how does KV/prefix caching actually reduce per-token costs in practice?
[00:03:21] Omar: sure. for assistants where users ask follow-ups, a lot of tokens are repeats — past few turns or system prompt. Redwood supports KV cache and a prefix cache. for example a 60% cache hit on prefix tokens means you only compute new tokens 40% of the time. combined with batching, your GPU is doing amortized work. so if your average call has 1,200 tokens but 700 are cached, you only generate 500 tokens — that directly scales down generation compute.
[00:03:44] Samir: what's a realistic cache hit rate for our use case? we do long summaries where input varies a lot.
[00:03:48] Omar: for summarization of documents the cache hit is lower, but we still see KV reuse for repeated system prompts or shared context like company policy text. realistic end-to-end savings maybe 1.5–2.5x for summarization workloads. for chat/assistant flows with reuse you can hit 3x-5x.

[00:04:05] Priya: batching — how much of our SLA will be affected if you batch to increase throughput? our product needs sub-300ms for short prompts sometimes.
[00:04:13] Omar: batching has tradeoffs. small batching windows (10–30ms) can increase GPU utilization with minimal latency impact; continuous batching in the runtime keeps tail latency stable. for very low-latency 100–200ms flows we recommend a separate low-latency route pinned to smaller models or dedicated low-latency pool, and route bulk/long jobs to high-throughput pool. Redwood supports routing policies for that.
[00:04:33] Maya: so architecture pattern is often hybrid: hosted or small dedicated low-latency for user-facing quick responses, and larger dedicated pools for high-throughput summarization.

[00:04:42] Lena: ok, can you show example pricing scenarios quickly? rough numbers are fine.
[00:04:46] Omar: sure. I'll present three scenarios assuming current token volume 600M/mo and target growth to 1.5B/mo in 6 months.
[00:04:53] Scenario A — Hosted naive: at $0.0008/token => 600M * 0.0008 = $480k/mo. Not viable.
[00:05:02] Scenario B — Hosted with caching & batching (effective reduction 4x): effective tokens billed ~150M => 150M * 0.0008 = $120k/mo. Still above $30k but much better; can be improved with model choice to $0.0004/token and higher cache hitting => ~60k/month.
[00:05:18] Scenario C — Dedicated reserved: a dedicated multi-GPU pod (example: 8xA10 equivalent) reserved with moderate utilization might cost $25k-$35k/mo for the infra plus Redwood platform fee; with 4x effective efficiency from batching/caching your 600M tokens could be served for in-range of $20k-$40k/mo depending on utilization and model.
[00:05:37] Maya: Important note: those dedicated numbers assume high utilization; if utilization is low it can be more expensive. we usually run utilization models in the quote. also we offer burst to hosted so you don't need to overprovision.

[00:05:48] Samir: what's included in the dedicated platform fee? and how big is the up-front commitment?
[00:05:52] Maya: Dedicated includes support, per-route tracing, rollouts, and priority capacity. commitment typically monthly or annual; discounts increase with annual commit. platform fee is a fixed amount per cluster reserve — example numbers we can provide in the pricing doc.

[00:06:05] Lena: private — one-time license + infra. rough ballpark compared to dedicated?
[00:06:09] Omar: Private has higher one-time setup and possible license fee (varies depending on compliance add-ons). infra cost depends on your data center/cloud choices; for large sustained volume often cheaper over 12+ months than dedicated because you own the hardware. but it requires infra ops.

[00:06:21] Priya: we need SOC2/ISO and KMS integration for keys. is that supported in Hosted? Dedicated? Private?
[00:06:28] Maya: Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit; for customer-managed KMS and SOC2 enterprise features we recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated can integrate with your KMS in many cases; Private gives you full on-prem control. we'll share the security pack.

[00:06:40] [00:06:40] Lena: any case studies where a customer hit our target $30k/mo?
[00:06:44] Omar: yes — a mid-market analytics company moved to Dedicated reserved pods, used 3x batching and 50% prefix caching and got down to an effective $0.0002-$0.00025/token equivalent, landing them in the $25k-$35k range for similar volume. we'll share anonymized benchmark.

[00:06:59] Maya: quick note on quantization: 4-bit quant models let you run on cheaper GPU SKUs and increase batch sizes; that often reduces effective infra cost by 20–40% at similar quality for many workloads.

[00:07:10] Priya: what's the expected time to get a dedicated pod up for pilot?
[00:07:13] Maya: from contract to provision usually 2–4 weeks depending on cloud region and sizing. we can do a hosted-backed pilot faster (days), or a hybrid where we provision a small dedicated pod and use hosted for overflow.

[00:07:25] Samir: ok, let's talk concrete pilot plan.
[00:07:28] Rachel: recommended pilot: 1-week dedicated pod with your production-like request mix, run Redwood benchmark script (we'll provide) comparing latency, throughput, and cost with and without caching. Redwood will run a parallel hosted fallback test.
[00:07:39] Priya: we can allocate a small budget for a week-long pilot. then we'll evaluate.

[00:07:44] Lena: about SLA: if we go dedicated, what uptime and latency SLAs are typical?
[00:07:48] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime targets; latency SLOs are a combination of model choice and pool sizing. we'll include example SLOs in the quote.

[00:07:55] [00:07:55] Samir: any gotchas — hidden costs or egress charges we need to factor?
[00:07:59] Omar: main things: network egress if cross-region, storage for large KV caches if you keep state long-term, and potential engineering time to integrate routing rules. we call these out in the estimate.

[00:08:10] Priya: for the pilot, what logs and metrics will you need from our side?
[00:08:14] Omar: sequence length distribution, request per second patterns, and a sample of prompts (sanitized) to run representative cache/benchmarks. also any latency SLOs for tail latencies.

[00:08:24] Lena: will you provide cost model spreadsheets? we like to see line-items.
[00:08:28] Maya: yes, we'll send a per-token spreadsheet modeling hosted, hosted-with-cache, dedicated at different utilization points, and private TCO examples.

[00:08:36] [00:08:36] (brief cross-talk, someone drops a word)
[00:08:40] Samir: can Redwood do dynamic routing so we put mission-critical traffic on dedicated low-latency and bulk jobs on high-throughput?
[00:08:46] Omar: absolutely — routing policies by route, model, or tag. automatic fallback to hosted when capacity is constrained.

[00:08:54] Lena: curious about billing granularity — is hosted billed per token as we talked, but dedicated billed as infra + platform fee. do you also bill for cache misses as separate?
[00:09:01] Maya: hosted is token billed. for dedicated you pay the reserved infra and platform fee; we don't double-bill tokens, though we may include a small request-level charge for very small requests in some pricing configurations — we'll detail that in the sheet. caching reduces compute and thus affects how many tokens you actually end up computing; we show both theoretical and effective billing lines.

[00:09:18] Priya: about SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM, SAML, and role separation between infra ops and product teams.
[00:09:24] Maya: supported on Dedicated and Private; Hosted has enterprise SSO features for orgs on enterprise plan. we'll attach the security and compliance docs.

[00:09:33] Lena: any quick wins you recommend to immediately reduce cost while we evaluate?
[00:09:36] Omar: yes — 1) reduce model size where acceptable (small model for short Q/A), 2) enable KV/prefix caching for interactions that reuse context, 3) batch non-interactive jobs, 4) quantize models to 4-bit where quality is acceptable. even small changes can drop cost 20–50% right away.

[00:09:51] Samir: Alright, sounds good. let's recap next steps.
[00:09:55] Maya: recap: we'll send pricing scenarios and a per-token cost model, Omar will share the benchmark script and caching best-practices, Priya will provide token distribution logs. Redwood will provision a small dedicated pod for a 1-week pilot week of 2026-07-20 if we can confirm.
[00:10:10] Priya: sounds good, I'll aim to get the logs by 2026-07-10.
[00:10:14] Lena: we'll review pricing and get back on commitment level.
[00:10:17] Maya: perfect. any other questions?
[00:10:20] Samir: none from me.
[00:10:21] Rachel: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot planning and share the security pack.
[00:10:25] Maya: thanks everyone.
[00:10:27] Lena: thanks folks.

[00:10:30] (call ends)
